title: Invoicing and billing setup for enterprise deals (POs, net terms, tax)
author: Rachel Kim
content:
## Purpose
This page documents the Finance steps and requirements that are part of the **end-to-end process for getting a non-standard enterprise deal approved and signed at Redwood Inference**.

Billing setup frequently blocks signature when procurement requires invoicing details, PO language, or vendor onboarding.

## When Finance must be engaged
Engage Finance (RevRec/Billing) when any of the following applies:
- Net terms > Net 30
- Customer requires a Purchase Order (PO)
- Customer requires vendor onboarding forms (W-9, bank letter, insurance certificates if applicable)
- Multi-year agreements with ramp schedules
- Any non-standard invoicing cadence (quarterly, monthly)

## Required billing fields (must be captured before signature)
- Bill-to legal entity
- Bill-to address
- Remit-to requirements (if customer mandates)
- Invoicing email / portal
- PO required (yes/no) and PO number if available
- Tax/VAT status and exemptions (if any)
- Payment terms requested (Net 30 default)

## Net terms policy
- **Default:** Net 30
- **Net 45:** Finance approval required
- **Net 60+ or any pay-when-paid language:** CFO approval required; generally avoided

## Invoicing cadence policy
- Annual upfront is preferred (especially for discounts)
- Quarterly is allowed with Finance approval
- Monthly invoicing is allowed only for usage-based Hosted API when standard; for Dedicated/Private it requires Finance approval

## PO requirements
- If customer requires a PO, ensure the Order Form explicitly states whether a PO is a precondition to invoicing.
- If customer requires PO before signature, AE must obtain it and attach it to the CRM record.

## RevRec considerations (high level)
Finance reviews for:
- Non-standard acceptance criteria
- Unusual termination rights or refundability
- Deliverables tied to roadmap
- Ramp schedules that change allocation of revenue

## Procedure (Billing setup)
1) AE/Deal Desk completes Deal Intake Form billing section.
2) Finance validates net terms and invoicing cadence.
3) Finance confirms whether tax/VAT applies and whether exemption documents are required.
4) Finance provides invoice instructions for inclusion in the Order Form if needed.
5) Before signature: Finance confirms Billing Approved in the deal record.

## Exit criteria
Billing setup is complete when:
- Payment terms are approved
- PO requirements are satisfied or clearly documented
- Invoicing contacts/addresses are recorded

## Common pitfalls
- Net terms negotiated verbally without Finance approval
- Missing bill-to entity causes re-papering late in procurement
- Monthly invoicing for Dedicated without approval increases collections risk
